tasks.old_behavior: The fmt_repl inner function receives the query tag key from the regex match and checks it directly against ALLOWED_QUERY_TAGS (all lowercase). If the key is uppercase (e.g., '%{NAME}'), it does not match any allowed tag and is passed through literally via brackets(). Only lowercase keys like '%{name}' are recognized and substituted with package attribute values.
tasks.new_behavior: The fmt_repl inner function calls key.lower() at the start, converting any uppercase tag to lowercase before checking against ALLOWED_QUERY_TAGS. Both '%{NAME}' and '%{name}' are now recognized and substituted with the corresponding package attribute value. The behavior for lowercase tags is unchanged; the return format string now uses the already-lowered key variable instead of calling .lower() again.
tasks.compatibility_reason: This patch restores support for uppercased query tags (e.g., '%{NAME}', '%{RELEASE}', '%{REPONAME}') that was unintentionally lost in commit e50488b6 (v4.15.0). Users who specify query tags in uppercase will now see the corresponding package attribute values instead of literal tag text. This is a backward-compatible relaxation of the input contract: existing lowercase-only inputs continue to work identically. The change mirrors rpm's behavior where both uppercase and lowercase query tags are accepted.
tasks.test_recommendation: Run tests.test_repoquery::OutputTest::test_output which exercises uppercase query tags. Also verify that the existing lowercase-based tests still pass. Regression-test that %{name} behavior is unchanged.
